title: Salvage, new arms and a new Talos
summary: Wars grew teeth and the sector gained new places, gear and arms. Invasions now combine several fleets, stations under attack call nearby allies for help, and new missions send you to protect stations, strike them, join fleets or hunt them. Destroyed ships and stations leave wrecks you can strip with a Salvage Rig. Jumps burn fuel, which stations sell and the Star Energizer draws from stars. Ringed planets have their rings as local spaces full of ice asteroids, miners and pirates. Modules sit around the ship's and automaton's picture, grouped by where they are fitted. Electro, the Bouncer Plasma, the Beam Emitter, the Cloak and the Projection Array join the Pulse Cannon. Saving gained six slots, saves on planets, quicksave, quickload and autosave. No page needs scrolling any more. Talos was reorganised around one navigation rail, with Versions at the top, and made fast: switching tools takes a millisecond or two. Every screen, Talos included, runs at 240 FPS or more.

steps.title: Wars that call for help
steps.text: Invasions now gather several fleets into one force before they strike. A station under attack sends a distress call, and allied fleets in nearby systems come to defend it, then go home when it's over. New missions use this: protect a station during an invasion, strike an enemy station, join a fleet, or hunt one down.

diagram.label:
INVASION
3 fleets gather
then strike together

STATION ATTACKED
sends a distress call

ALLIED FLEETS
in nearby systems
come to defend

diagram.text: allies go home when the fight is won

steps.title: Wrecks and salvage
steps.text: Destroyed ships and stations now leave a wreck: the same hull, greyed out and scarred, drifting where it died. With a Salvage Rig fitted you can strip it for parts, cargo and sometimes the weapons it carried, Electro included.

diagram.text: a wreck shader: grey, burnt, cracked

steps.title: Fuel and the Star Energizer
steps.text: Ships now burn fuel to jump between systems, and every hull has its own tank. Stations sell fuel, the Fuel Tank module carries more, and an empty tank leaves you crawling at a third of your speed. The Star Energizer refuels you for free near a star by drawing on its power.

diagram.label:
STAR ENERGIZER
free fuel near a star

steps.title: Rings you can fly into
steps.text: Ringed planets now have their rings as places of their own: dense fields of ice asteroids you collide with, where NPC miners work and pirates hunt them. Defending the miners earns favour with their empire. This kind of pocket is now called local space, beside planet space, solar space and galaxy space (reached only through the galaxy map).

diagram.text: defend the miners: favour with their empire
local space · planet space · solar space · galaxy space

steps.title: Equipment on the body
steps.text: Modules are no longer slots laid over the picture. The ship and the automaton each show their picture with slots around it, grouped by where the module sits: the nose, wings, hull, thrusters and bay of a ship, or the head, arms and legs of the automaton. The slots line up evenly, keep the same gap from the picture, and never cover it.

diagram.text: the same gap all round · never over the picture

steps.title: Four new weapons
steps.text: Electro throws lightning that jumps from enemy to enemy and can stun them; NPCs carry it too, and you can salvage it. The Bouncer Plasma ball bounces between enemies, hurting each one, then webs them together and slows them. An enemy's Bouncer webs you to its ships. The Beam Emitter fires a continuous beam that drains shields fast but does little to hulls. The starting gun is now the Pulse Cannon, which hits shields and hull evenly.

diagram.label:
BOUNCER
bounces, then webs
and slows

BEAM EMITTER
shields x2.0
hull x0.35

diagram.text: Electro jumping from ship to ship
NPCs carry them; salvage them from wrecks

steps.title: The Cloak and the Projection Array
steps.text: The Cloak makes your ship see-through and invisible to enemies until you fire. While cloaked your shields are down, and they take 2 seconds to return afterwards. A shimmering, light-bending edge shows on the hull. The Projection Array makes two illusions of your ship that fly beside you; each vanishes when shot, and every few seconds you swap places with one of them.

diagram.label:
CLOAK
invisible until you fire
shields down · back in 2 s

PROJECTION ARRAY
two illusions beside you
shot: gone · you swap places

steps.title: Saves: slots, planets, quick and auto
steps.text: Saving now has six slots, each showing where you were, your ship and your credits. A save made on a planet's surface loads you back there, standing where you were. F5 quicksaves and F9 quickloads. Autosaves happen every few minutes (not mid-fight) and when you dock, arrive in a system or land; Settings > Game sets how often, or turns them off.

diagram.label:
ON A PLANET
loads you back there

AUTOSAVE
every 2-30 min (Settings > Game) · not mid-fight
and on docking, arriving, landing

diagram.text: never lose more than a few minutes

steps.title: Screens that fit
steps.text: No page needs scrolling at 1920 x 1080: the inventory, outfitting, shipyard, missions, sell lists and controls were laid out again in columns and card grids. Items in the cargo hold have tooltips. A Spartan missions board that ran at 20 FPS now draws its comms portraits once and runs at over 470.

diagram.label:
BEFORE
one long column
scroll to see it all

NOW
columns and card grids
everything in view

steps.title: Talos, reorganised
steps.text: Every Talos screen now has one rail down the left: Versions (the patch notes, renamed from the Patcher) at the top, then the Library with its new bookshelf icon, the data editor's pages and the other tools. The rail never moves or resizes. Each screen has a one-line header, and the dialogue editor fits a whole stage without scrolling. Versions always opens on the newest version's infographic.

diagram.label: NAME   ·   what it's for   ·   its buttons

THE TOOL
a whole stage on one screen · no hub to go back through

steps.title: Talos at full speed
steps.text: Each tool is built the first time you open it and then kept, so switching takes a millisecond or two and never loses your work. Symbol fonts are bundled, so text with arrows or ticks no longer waits on the system to find a font for them. The galaxy for the editors is generated without its economy, icons are painted once and cached, and the half-second file check of live coding is spread across frames. Talos is now part of the frame-rate tour: 21 scenarios, all above 240 FPS.

diagram.label:
SYMBOL FONTS
bundled: no lookup
361 ms to 66 ms

ICONS
painted once
kept on disk

review.intro: A long session in three parts: the game (wars that call for help, wrecks and salvage, fuel, the rings' local spaces, equipment screens by area, five new arms, save slots and autosaves, pages that never scroll), Talos (one navigation rail, every tool kept alive, Versions at the top) and speed (bundled symbol fonts, baked portraits and icons, the live-coding watcher spread out, the Library's rocks through staggered views - 91 tour scenarios, none under 240 FPS). New scripts: chain_lightning, plasma_bouncer, projection_array, wreck, equip_doll and talos_nav.

files.explanation: A 170 KB subset of DejaVu Sans: arrows, maths symbols, box drawing, geometric shapes (▲ ▼ ◀ ▶ ●), dingbats (✓ ✕) and Greek. The game's own fonts lack these; without this fallback every text holding one asked the system's fontconfig for a font each time it was laid out (three quarters of the Scenario Editor's build time).

A 28 KB subset of Noto Sans Math for the two arrows DejaVu lacks (⤒ ⤓), its line metrics made compact (ascent 900, descent 230) - Godot measures a font's line height over its fallbacks too, and the original tall metrics made every line in the game 4 px taller.
The licence shipped with the Noto Sans Math subset.

files.explanation: The Electro weapon's lightning: it strikes its target at once and leaps on to nearby ships of the same side, each hit weaker, each may be stunned. Ships of every side can fit it.

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,114 @@ 
+class_name ChainLightning
+extends Node2D
+## The Electro weapon's lightning (Items.WEAPONS "electro"): a bolt that
+## strikes its target at once and leaps on to the nearest other ship of the
+## same side within `leap`, up to `chain` more, each hit `falloff` of the
+## last. Electric damage (Gear: "electric"); each ship hit may be stunned for
+## a moment (stun(): it drifts, its guns silent). The player's ship and NPC
+## ships fit it alike (an NPC with `electro` fires it instead of bolts).
+##
+## The node itself is the flash: jagged lines between the hits, re-jagged as
+## it flickers, gone in LIFE seconds. Cheap - a handful of polylines.
+
+const LIFE := 0.3
+
+var _points: PackedVector2Array      # the hits, in order (global)
+var _t := 0.0
+var _color := Color(0.6, 0.8, 1.0)
+var _rng := RandomNumberGenerator.new()
+
+
+## Strikes `first` from `from` (the firer, null for a hazard): returns the
+## ships hit. `w`: the weapon's stats (Items.WEAPONS["electro"]), `damage`
+## its first hit (tech and modules applied by the firer).
+static func strike(tree: SceneTree, from: Node2D, first: Node2D, damage: float, w: Dictionary) -> Array:
+	if not is_instance_valid(first):
+		return []
+	var group: StringName = first.faction_group() if first.has_method("faction_group") else &"enemies"
+	if first.is_in_group("player"):
+		group = &"player"
+	var hit: Array = [first]
+	var pts := PackedVector2Array([from.global_position if is_instance_valid(from) else first.global_position, first.global_position])
+	var d := damage
+	_hit(first, d, from, w)
+	var at: Node2D = first
+	for i in int(w.get("chain", 3)):
+		var best: Node2D = null
+		var best_d: float = w.get("leap", 420.0)
+		for n in tree.get_nodes_in_group(group):
+			if n in hit or not is_instance_valid(n) or not n is Node2D or (n.has_method("is_alive") and not n.is_alive()):
+				continue
+			if n.get("untouchable") == true or not _foe_of(from, n):
+				continue
+			var dd: float = n.global_position.distance_to(at.global_position)
+			if dd < best_d:
+				best = n
+				best_d = dd
+		if best == null:
+			break
+		d *= float(w.get("falloff", 0.75))
+		_hit(best, d, from, w)
+		hit.append(best)
+		pts.append(best.global_position)
+		at = best
+	var fx := ChainLightning.new()
+	fx._points = pts
+	fx._color = w.get("color", Color(0.6, 0.8, 1.0))
+	var host: Node = tree.get_first_node_in_group("fx_layer")
+	if host == null:
+		host = from.get_parent() if is_instance_valid(from) else first.get_parent()
+	host.add_child(fx)
+	Sfx.play_world("space/hazard_zap", first.global_position, -2.0, 0.15)
+	return hit
+
+
+## Would `from`'s lightning leap to `n`? Only to its foes: from you, to
+## hostile ships (not the neutrals minding their business); from an NPC, not
+## to its own empire's ships.
+static func _foe_of(from: Node2D, n: Node2D) -> bool:
+	if not is_instance_valid(from):
+		return true
+	if from.is_in_group("player"):
+		return not (n.has_method("is_neutral") and n.is_neutral() and not n.is_hostile_to_player())
+	var fe = from.get("empire")
+	var ne = n.get("empire")
+	if fe is String and ne is String and fe != "" and fe == ne:
+		return false
+	return true
+
+
+static func _hit(n: Node2D, dmg: float, from: Node2D, w: Dictionary) -> void:
+	if n.has_method("take_damage"):
+		n.take_damage(dmg, from.global_position if is_instance_valid(from) else n.global_position, from if is_instance_valid(from) else null, "electric")
+	if is_instance_valid(n) and n.has_method("stun") and randf() < float(w.get("stun", 0.25)):
+		n.stun(float(w.get("stun_time", 1.5)))
+
+
+func _ready() -> void:
+	z_index = 5
+	_rng.randomize()
+
+
+func _process(delta: float) -> void:
+	_t += delta
+	if _t >= LIFE:
+		queue_free()
+		return
+	queue_redraw()
+
+
+func _draw() -> void:
+	var a := 1.0 - _t / LIFE
+	for i in _points.size() - 1:
+		var p0 := _points[i]
+		var p1 := _points[i + 1]
+		var line := PackedVector2Array([p0])
+		var n := maxi(3, int(p0.distance_to(p1) / 45.0))
+		var side := (p1 - p0).orthogonal().normalized()
+		for k in range(1, n):
+			line.append(p0.lerp(p1, float(k) / n) + side * _rng.randf_range(-18.0, 18.0))
+		line.append(p1)
+		draw_polyline(line, Color(_color, 0.35 * a), 9.0)
+		draw_polyline(line, Color(_color.lightened(0.5), 0.9 * a), 3.0)
+		draw_polyline(line, Color(1, 1, 1, a), 1.2)
+		draw_circle(p1, 14.0 * a, Color(_color, 0.5 * a))

+class_name EquipDoll
+extends Control
+## An equipment screen in the manner of action RPGs: the ship (or the
+## automaton - you on a planet) drawn large in the middle, and round it its
+## areas' slots - each group placed beside its area and joined to it by a
+## line. Ships: nose, wings, hull, thrusters, cargo bay (Shipyard.AREAS);
+## the automaton: head, back, torso, arms, hand, legs (Gear.AREA_OF_SLOT).
+## The slots are ItemSlots made by the page that shows the doll (it knows
+## what dragging onto them and right-clicking them does):
+##   var d := EquipDoll.new()
+##   d.picture = tex
+##   d.add_group("nose", "NOSE", Vector2(0.5, 0.0), Vector2(0.5, 0.1), false, [slot, slot])
+## `at`: where the group sits in the doll (0..1 each way: its edge-most
+## point); `anchor`: the spot it belongs to on the picture (0..1 of it);
+## vertical: the slots stacked (else side by side).
+
+const MAX_RUN := 4

+func add_group(key: String, title: String, at: Vector2, anchor: Vector2, vertical: bool, slots: Array) -> void:
+	# Up to MAX_RUN slots in a line; more (an over-full area) wrap into more lines.
+	var box := GridContainer.new()
+	box.columns = (ceili(slots.size() / float(MAX_RUN)) if vertical else mini(slots.size(), MAX_RUN)) if not slots.is_empty() else 1
+	box.add_theme_constant_override("h_separation", 3)
+	box.add_theme_constant_override("v_separation", 3)
+	var cap := UI.label(title, 11, NeonTheme.HEAD)
+	cap.horizontal_alignment = HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_CENTER
+	var holder := VBoxContainer.new()

+func _notification(what: int) -> void:

+func _layout() -> void:
+	# The picture in the middle, as big as fits once the slot groups have
+	# room round it; every group then sits the same distance (GAP) from the
+	# picture's frame: left groups just left of it, right ones just right, the
+	# top one just above, the bottom one just below - each along that side at
+	# its own spot (`at`).
+	var left := 0.0
+	var right := 0.0
+	var top := 0.0
+	var bottom := 0.0

+			"right": right = maxf(right, ms.x)

+			"bottom": bottom = maxf(bottom, ms.y)

+	var h := minf(size.y * picture_scale, size.y - top - bottom - room * 2.0)
+	var w := h * aspect
+	var max_w := size.x - maxf(left, right) * 2.0 - room * 2.0   # (centred: room for the wider side on both)
+	if w > max_w:
+		w = max_w
+		h = w / aspect
+	w = maxf(w, 10.0)
+	h = maxf(h, 10.0)
+	var cy := top + room + (size.y - top - bottom - room * 2.0) / 2.0
+	_pic_rect = Rect2(Vector2(size.x / 2.0 - w / 2.0, cy - h / 2.0), Vector2(w, h))
+	var frame := _pic_rect.grow(FRAME)
+	# Along each side: each group at its own spot, then spread so none overlap
+	# (in order; pulled back inside the doll if they run past its edge).
+	var sides := {"left": [], "right": [], "top": [], "bottom": []}
+	for g in groups:
+		sides[_side(g)].append(g)
+	for side in sides:
+		var along_y: bool = side in ["left", "right"]
+		var lo: float = frame.position.y if along_y else frame.position.x
+		var hi: float = frame.end.y if along_y else frame.end.x
+		var items := []
+		var thick := 0.0   # the side's widest (left / right) or tallest (top / bottom) group: all made that size
+		for g in sides[side]:
+			var ms: Vector2 = (g["box"] as Control).get_combined_minimum_size()
+			thick = maxf(thick, ms.x if along_y else ms.y)
+			items.append([0.0, ms.y if along_y else ms.x, g, ms, Vector2(g["at"]).y if along_y else Vector2(g["at"]).x])
+		items.sort_custom(func(a, b): return a[4] < b[4])
+		# Evenly spread along the frame's side (equal space between them and
+		# at the ends); with too little room, stacked SPREAD apart.
+		var total := 0.0
+		for it in items:
+			total += it[1]
+		var free_len: float = (hi - lo) - total
+		var step: float = free_len / (items.size() + 1) if free_len > SPREAD * (items.size() + 1) else SPREAD
+		var cur: float = lo + step if free_len > SPREAD * (items.size() + 1) else lo + (hi - lo - total - SPREAD * (items.size() - 1)) / 2.0
+		for it in items:
+			it[0] = cur
+			cur += it[1] + step
+			# (every group on the side as wide - or as tall - as the biggest: their slots share a centre line)
+			it[3] = Vector2(thick, it[3].y) if along_y else Vector2(it[3].x, thick)
+		var limit: float = size.y if along_y else size.x
+		if not items.is_empty() and items[0][0] < 0.0:
+			var under: float = -items[0][0]
+			for it in items:
+				it[0] += under
+		if not items.is_empty() and items[-1][0] + items[-1][1] > limit:
+			var over: float = items[-1][0] + items[-1][1] - limit
+			for it in items:
+				it[0] = maxf(0.0, it[0] - over)
+		for it in items:
+			var ms: Vector2 = it[3]
+			var pos := Vector2.ZERO
+			match side:
+				"left": pos = Vector2(frame.position.x - GAP - ms.x, it[0])
+				"right": pos = Vector2(frame.end.x + GAP, it[0])
+				"top": pos = Vector2(it[0], frame.position.y - GAP - ms.y)
+				_: pos = Vector2(it[0], frame.end.y + GAP)
+			var box: Control = it[2]["box"]
+			box.position = pos.clamp(Vector2.ZERO, (size - ms).max(Vector2.ZERO))
+			box.size = ms

+## Which side of the picture a group sits on (from its `at`).
+func _side(g: Dictionary) -> String:
+	var at := Vector2(g["at"])
+	if at.x <= 0.05:

+	if at.x >= 0.95:

+## The point a group's line leaves from (the side of its box facing the picture).
+func _box_point(g: Dictionary) -> Vector2:
+	var box: Control = g["box"]

+	return Vector2(p.x, r.end.y if p.y < c.y else r.position.y)
+
+

+# Each icon is drawn once into a small texture (icon_texture: off screen, a
+# SubViewport) and the inventories' slots draw that: a page of slots (the
+# outfitter's 70 cards) costs one draw call a slot instead of half a dozen.
+# Until a texture is ready - and with no renderer (headless) - the slots draw
+# the icon itself (draw_icon).
+
+const ICON_BAKE := 64
+static var _icon_tex := {}         # "id|dim" -> Texture2D, or null while baking / when it can't be
+static var _icon_queue: Array = []
+static var _icon_baking := false
+
+
+class IconDraw extends Control:
+	var id := ""
+	var dim := false
+	func _draw() -> void:
+		Items.draw_icon(self, id, Rect2(Vector2.ZERO, size), dim)
+
+
+static func icon_texture(id: String, dim := false) -> Texture2D:
+	var key := "%s|%s" % [id, dim]
+	if _icon_tex.has(key):
+		return _icon_tex[key]
+	_icon_tex[key] = null
+	_icon_queue.append([key, id, dim])
+	if not _icon_baking:
+		_bake_icons.call_deferred()
+	return null
+
+
+static func _bake_icons() -> void:
+	var tree := Engine.get_main_loop() as SceneTree
+	if tree == null or _icon_queue.is_empty():
+		return
+	_icon_baking = true
+	var jobs := _icon_queue.duplicate()
+	_icon_queue.clear()
+	var vps := []
+	for j in jobs:
+		var vp := SubViewport.new()
+		vp.size = Vector2i(ICON_BAKE, ICON_BAKE)
+		vp.transparent_bg = true
+		vp.render_target_update_mode = SubViewport.UPDATE_ONCE
+		var d := IconDraw.new()
+		d.id = j[1]
+		d.dim = j[2]
+		d.size = Vector2(ICON_BAKE, ICON_BAKE)
+		vp.add_child(d)
+		tree.root.add_child(vp)
+		vps.append(vp)
+	await RenderingServer.frame_post_draw
+	await RenderingServer.frame_post_draw
+	for i in jobs.size():
+		var img: Image = vps[i].get_texture().get_image()
+		vps[i].queue_free()
+		if img != null and not img.is_empty():
+			img.generate_mipmaps()
+			_icon_tex[jobs[i][0]] = ImageTexture.create_from_image(img)
+	_icon_baking = false
+	tree.call_group("item_slots", "queue_redraw")
+	if not _icon_queue.is_empty():

 ## The watched files' times; changed ones are hot reloaded (first = just record).
+## The watcher, a little each frame: listing a folder or checking files'
+## times for at most SCAN_BUDGET_MS, then on next frame - a whole pass
+## (some 9 ms of file checks) all at once stuttered the game twice a second.
+## A pass every 0.5 s at most; what changed is reloaded at the end of it.
+const SCAN_BUDGET_MS := 0.3
+var _queue: Array = []     # ["dir", path] / ["sheets", path] / ["file", path] / ["sheet", path, name]
+var _found: Array = []     # changed scripts this pass
+var _qi := 0
+
+func _watch_step(delta: float) -> void:
+	if _qi >= _queue.size():
+		_watch_t -= delta
+		if _watch_t > 0.0:
+			return
+		_watch_t = 0.5
+		_queue = []
+		_qi = 0
+		for d in watch_dirs:
+			_queue.append(["dir", d])
+		_queue.append(["sheets", SHEETS_DIR])
+	var t0 := Time.get_ticks_usec()
+	while _qi < _queue.size() and Time.get_ticks_usec() - t0 < SCAN_BUDGET_MS * 1000.0:
+		var w: Array = _queue[_qi]
+		_qi += 1
+		match w[0]:
+			"dir":
+				for f in DirAccess.get_files_at(w[1]):
+					if WATCH_EXT.has(f.get_extension()):
+						_queue.append(["file", str(w[1]).path_join(f)])
+			"sheets":
+				for f in DirAccess.get_files_at(w[1]):
+					if f.contains(SHEET_MATCH) and f.get_extension() == "png":
+						_queue.append(["sheet", str(w[1]).path_join(f), f])
+			"file":
+				var tm := FileAccess.get_modified_time(w[1])
+				if _mtimes.get(w[1], -1) != tm:   # (changed, or new)
+					_found.append(w[1])
+				_mtimes[w[1]] = tm
+			"sheet":
+				var tm := FileAccess.get_modified_time(w[1])
+				if _mtimes.get(w[1], -1) != tm and not _cutting.has(w[2]):
+					_cut_sheet(w[2])
+				_mtimes[w[1]] = tm
+	if _qi >= _queue.size() and not _found.is_empty():
+		var changed := _found
+		_found = []
+		reload(changed)
+
+

+## The symbols the UI uses (arrows ▲ ▼ ◀ ▶, ✓ ✕, ●, ─, Greek capitals...)
+## that the game's fonts don't have, from two small bundled fonts: without
+## them every piece of text holding one asked the system's fontconfig for a
+## font that has it - each time it was laid out (a rule card in the Scenario
+## Editor: ~60 ms, three quarters of it in fontconfig). Given to the default
+## font and to every bundled one, so text finds them before the system.
+const SYMBOL_FONTS := ["res://assets/fonts/DejaVuSans-Symbols.ttf", "res://assets/fonts/NotoSansMath-Arrows.ttf"]
+static var _fallbacks_done := false
+
+static func install_fallbacks() -> void:
+	if _fallbacks_done:
+		return
+	_fallbacks_done = true
+	var syms: Array[Font] = []
+	for path in SYMBOL_FONTS:
+		var f: Font = load(path)
+		if f:
+			syms.append(f)
+	var fonts: Array = [ThemeDB.fallback_font]
+	for path in ["res://assets/fonts/Rajdhani-Bold.ttf", "res://assets/fonts/Rajdhani-SemiBold.ttf", "res://assets/fonts/NotoSans-Black.ttf"]:
+		fonts.append(load(path))
+	for f in fonts:
+		if f is Font and f.fallbacks.is_empty():
+			f.fallbacks = syms
+
+
 static func build() -> Theme:
+	install_fallbacks()
 	if _theme != null:
 		return _theme
 	var t := Theme.new()

@@ -1,0 +1,237 @@ 
+class_name PlasmaBouncer
+extends Node2D
+## The Bouncer Plasma weapon (Items.WEAPONS "bouncer"): a ball of plasma that
+## flies at its target, hits it (heat damage) and bounces on to the nearest
+## enemy it hasn't hit yet (when it has hit them all, back to the nearest -
+## never straight back to the one it just left: between two it ping-pongs) -
+## up to `bounces` hits, each its full damage. When it's done
+## (its last bounce, or no enemy left in reach) it bursts into a PlasmaWeb
+## that ties every ship it hit together for `web_time` seconds - an enemy's
+## (NPCs carry it too: Enemy.bouncer) ties you to the ship that fired it and
+## up to two of its wingmen - slowed to
+## `web_slow` of their speed, none able to drift further than the web's
+## reach from the others (Enemy.web: they're pulled back in).
+##   PlasmaBouncer.fire(tree, ship, target, damage, Items.WEAPONS["bouncer"])
+
+const HIT_REACH := 14.0
+
+var w: Dictionary
+var damage := 20.0
+var shooter: Node2D
+var target: Node2D
+var _last: Node2D
+var _hits := 0
+var _hit: Array = []          # every ship it hit (the web's members)
+var _speed := 700.0
+var _vel := Vector2.ZERO
+var _t := 0.0
+var _trail: Array = []        # recent positions (the glow behind it)
+
+
+static func fire(tree: SceneTree, from: Node2D, first: Node2D, dmg: float, weapon: Dictionary) -> PlasmaBouncer:
+	var b := PlasmaBouncer.new()
+	b.w = weapon
+	b.damage = dmg
+	b.shooter = from
+	b.target = first
+	b._speed = float(weapon.get("speed", 700.0))
+	var host: Node = tree.get_first_node_in_group("fx_layer")
+	if host == null:
+		host = from.get_parent()
+	host.add_child(b)
+	b.global_position = from.global_position
+	b._vel = from.global_position.direction_to(first.global_position) * b._speed
+	Sfx.play_world("space/plasma", from.global_position, -2.0, 0.1)
+	return b
+
+
+func _ready() -> void:
+	z_index = 4
+
+
+func _process(delta: float) -> void:
+	_t += delta
+	if _t > 8.0:   # (lost: burst where it is)
+		_burst()
+		return
+	if not _alive(target):
+		target = _next_target()
+		if target == null:
+			_burst()
+			return
+	# Homing hard on its target (a ball of plasma, not a bolt).
+	var to := target.global_position - global_position
+	_vel = _vel.lerp(to.normalized() * _speed, minf(1.0, delta * 9.0))
+	global_position += _vel * delta
+	_trail.push_front(global_position)
+	if _trail.size() > 10:
+		_trail.pop_back()
+	if to.length() < float(target.get("hit_radius") if target.get("hit_radius") != null else 30.0) + HIT_REACH:
+		_strike(target)
+	if UI.redraw_due(self):
+		queue_redraw()
+
+
+func _strike(n: Node2D) -> void:
+	if n.has_method("take_damage"):
+		n.take_damage(damage, global_position, shooter if is_instance_valid(shooter) else null, "heat")
+	Effects.debris(global_position, Color(0.6, 1.0, 0.7), 0.4)
+	Sfx.play_world("space/plasma", global_position, -6.0, 0.25)
+	_hits += 1
+	if not n in _hit:
+		_hit.append(n)
+	_last = n
+	if _hits >= int(w.get("bounces", 6)):
+		_burst()
+		return
+	target = _next_target()
+	if target == null:
+		_burst()
+
+
+## The next to bounce to: the nearest enemy within reach it hasn't hit yet;
+## every one near hit already - the nearest but the one it just left.
+func _next_target() -> Node2D:
+	var fresh: Node2D = null
+	var fresh_d: float = float(w.get("leap", 460.0))
+	var again: Node2D = null
+	var again_d: float = fresh_d
+	var from := global_position
+	for g in [&"enemies", &"neutrals", &"player"]:
+		for n in get_tree().get_nodes_in_group(g):
+			if n == _last or n == shooter or not _alive(n) or not ChainLightning._foe_of(shooter, n) or n.get("untouchable") == true:
+				continue
+			var d: float = n.global_position.distance_to(from)
+			if not n in _hit and d < fresh_d:
+				fresh = n
+				fresh_d = d
+			elif n in _hit and d < again_d:
+				again = n
+				again_d = d
+	return fresh if fresh != null else again
+
+
+static func _alive(n) -> bool:
+	return is_instance_valid(n) and n is Node2D and (not n.has_method("is_alive") or n.is_alive())
+
+
+## Done bouncing: the ships it hit are webbed together.
+func _burst() -> void:
+	var members := _hit.filter(func(n): return _alive(n))
+	# An enemy's ball: what it hit (you) is webbed to the ship that fired it
+	# and its wingmen nearby - tethered to them, slowed.
+	if not members.is_empty() and _alive(shooter) and not shooter.is_in_group("player"):
+		members.append(shooter)
+		var mates := []
+		var e = shooter.get("empire")

@@ -1,0 +1,191 @@ 
+class_name ProjectionArray
+extends Node2D
+## The Projection Array (equipment, a toolbar system): it projects two
+## illusions of your ship that fly in formation beside you - the same hull,
+## heading and engines, nothing to tell them apart. Enemies can't tell either:
+## every ship attacking you picks one of the three at random, and so does one
+## that turns on you while they're up (Enemy._choose_target). An illusion is
+## gone the moment anything hits it (a flicker and it's nothing). Every
+## SHUFFLE seconds your ship swaps places with one of them - a flash on all
+## three hides it - so you can't be followed by where you were. They last
+## LIFE seconds at most.
+##   ProjectionArray.project(ship)
+
+const LIFE := 15.0
+const SHUFFLE := 4.0
+const SPACING := 170.0
+
+var ship: Node2D
+var decoys: Array = []
+var _t := 0.0
+var _shuffle_t := SHUFFLE
+
+
+static func project(ship: Node2D) -> ProjectionArray:
+	for old in ship.get_tree().get_nodes_in_group("projection_arrays"):
+		old.end()   # (a fresh pair replaces the old)
+	var pa := ProjectionArray.new()
+	pa.ship = ship
+	ship.get_parent().add_child(pa)
+	for side in [-1.0, 1.0]:
+		var d := Decoy.new()
+		d.ship = ship
+		d.offset = Vector2(side * SPACING, 40.0)
+		pa.add_child(d)
+		pa.decoys.append(d)
+		d.global_position = ship.global_position + d.offset.rotated(ship.rotation)
+	# Whoever was shooting at you now takes its pick of the three.
+	for e in ship.get_tree().get_nodes_in_group("enemies") + ship.get_tree().get_nodes_in_group("neutrals"):
+		if e.get("_target") == ship:
+			e._target = pa.pick(ship)
+	pa._flash_all()
+	Sfx.play_world("space/scan_pulse", ship.global_position, -3.0, 0.15)

files.explanation: Talos's navigation rail: every tool by icon and name down the left of every Talos screen, the same size and place everywhere, with the tools' shortcuts.

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,218 @@ 
+class_name TalosNav
+extends RefCounted
+## Talos's navigation rail: one column down the left of every Talos screen
+## listing every tool by icon and name - Versions (the patch notes) at the
+## top, then the Library, the data editor's pages (Dialogue, Chapters, Lore,
+## Citizens, Sprites), then the tools (Scenarios, SVG) and, at the foot, the way out to the title screen. The tool
+## you're in is lit. Click another and you're there - no going back to a hub
+## first (each screen asks about unsaved changes before it lets you go).
+##   var root := TalosNav.wrap(UI.modal(...), "svg", func(id): _guard(func(): TalosNav.open(get_tree(), id)))
+##   (the screen's own header and body then go in `root`)
+
+const EDITOR := "res://editor.tscn"
+const MENU := "res://main_menu.tscn"
+## The rail's size, the same on every screen: it never moves or resizes
+## (fixed font, text clipped, never scaled by the text-size setting).
+const WIDTH := 92
+const ITEM_H := 64
+## Where it sits on screen (the full-screen frames' inside corner; the
+## Library places its own rail there too).
+const AT := Vector2(44, 44)
+
+## [id, name, icon, keys, what it is]; "" separates the groups.
+const TOOLS := [
+	["patcher", "Versions", "patch", "F7", "Every version of the game and its patches: what each brought, as a one-paragraph summary\nand a step-by-step animated infographic (opens on the newest), with the code review behind it."],
+	["library", "Library", "library", "F3", "Every asset of the game, alive, in rooms: characters walking and fighting, ships, stations,\nplanets, buildings and effects - to preview everything in one place."],
+	"",
+	["dialogue", "Dialogue", "dialogue", "Ctrl+1", "Each stage of the main quest: its objective, rewards and the dialogue\nthat plays when it starts. Preview the dialogue in the game's own box."],
+	["chapters", "Chapters", "ui_journal", "Ctrl+2", "The titles of the main quest's chapters, as shown in the Ship Computer."],
+	["lore", "Lore", "lore", "Ctrl+3", "The lore entries the player unlocks during the quest (titles and BBCode text)."],
+	["citizens", "Citizens", "chat", "Ctrl+4", "What Minoan citizens say when you click them: the Minoan words\nand their translation (shown in the event log)."],
+	["sprites", "Sprites", "sprites", "Ctrl+5", "Every sprite of the game by group (hover one for its key and file).\nReload them after re-cutting the reference sheets."],
+	"",
+	["scenarios", "Scenarios", "quest", "F4", "Quests written as plain-sentence rules: WHEN something happens AND these are true\nTHEN do these - every word picked from a drop-down. Test them in a new game."],
+	["svg", "SVG", "svg", "F6", "A vector drawing program: shapes, Bezier paths, freehand, text, fill and stroke, nodes,\nlayers of objects. Opens and saves SVG files and exports PNG images at any size."],
+]
+## The data editor's pages, in TOOLS order (DevMode.TABS).
+const PAGES := ["dialogue", "chapters", "lore", "citizens", "sprites"]
+const SCENES := {"scenarios": "res://scenario_editor.tscn", "library": "res://zoo.tscn",
+	"svg": "res://svg_editor.tscn", "patcher": "res://patcher.tscn", "menu": MENU}
+
+## The data editor's page to open on (set when another tool sends you to one).
+static var page := 0
+
+
+## The rail, `current` lit; clicking a tool calls go(id) ("menu": the title screen).
+## `keys`: the rail also answers the tools' shortcuts (Ctrl+1-5, F3, F4, F6, F7)
+## - not for the data editor, which has its own.
+static func rail(current: String, go: Callable, keys := true) -> VBoxContainer:
+	_warm()
+	var box := VBoxContainer.new()
+	box.name = "TalosNav"
+	if keys:
+		var k := Keys.new()
+		k.go = go
+		k.current = current
+		box.add_child(k)
+	box.custom_minimum_size.x = WIDTH
+	box.size_flags_horizontal = Control.SIZE_SHRINK_BEGIN
+	box.set_meta("fixed_font", true)   # (UI.scale_fonts leaves it alone)
+	box.add_theme_constant_override("separation", 4)
+	for t in TOOLS:
+		if t is String:
+			var sep := HSeparator.new()
+			sep.add_theme_constant_override("separation", 10)
+			box.add_child(sep)
+			continue
+		box.add_child(_item(t[0], t[1], t[2], EditorIcons.tip(t[1], t[3], t[4]), go))
+	var gap := Control.new()
+	gap.size_flags_vertical = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
+	box.add_child(gap)
+	box.add_child(_item("menu", "Exit", "exit", EditorIcons.tip("Exit Talos", "", "Back to the title screen. Each tool asks about unsaved changes first;\nedits already made apply to games started from here on.")
+		, go))
+	select(box, current)
+	return box
+
+
+static func _item(id: String, name: String, icon: String, tip: String, go: Callable) -> Button:
+	var b := Button.new()
+	b.name = "Nav_" + id
+	b.text = name
+	b.icon = EditorIcons.get_icon(icon)
+	b.icon_alignment = HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_CENTER
+	b.vertical_icon_alignment = VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT_TOP
+	b.toggle_mode = true
+	b.focus_mode = Control.FOCUS_NONE
+	b.custom_minimum_size = Vector2(WIDTH, ITEM_H)
+	b.clip_text = true   # (a long name can't widen the rail)
+	b.text_overrun_behavior = TextServer.OVERRUN_TRIM_ELLIPSIS
+	b.add_theme_font_size_override("font_size", 13)
+	b.tooltip_text = tip
+	b.set_meta("talos_nav", id)
+	b.pressed.connect(func():
+		select(b.get_parent(), str(b.get_parent().get_meta("current", "")))   # (lit only when you get there)
+		go.call(id))
+	return b
+
+
+## The tools' scenes, loaded in the background once Talos is open, so the
+## first visit to each doesn't wait for its scripts and scene to load
+## (~0.4-1 s the first time; then they're ready).
+static func _warm() -> void:
+	if DisplayServer.get_name() == "headless":
+		return
+	for path in [EDITOR] + SCENES.values():
+		if path != MENU and not ResourceLoader.has_cached(path) and ResourceLoader.load_threaded_get_status(path) == ResourceLoader.THREAD_LOAD_INVALID_RESOURCE:
+			ResourceLoader.load_threaded_request(path)
+
+
+## Lights `current`'s button.
+static func select(box: Node, current: String) -> void:
+	box.set_meta("current", current)
+	for b in box.get_children():
+		if b is Button:
+			b.set_pressed_no_signal(b.get_meta("talos_nav", "") == current)
+
+
+## The rail beside a screen's content: `root` (a full-screen modal's box)
+## gets the rail and a column for the screen, which is returned.
+static func wrap(root: VBoxContainer, current: String, go: Callable, keys := true) -> VBoxContainer:
+	var row := HBoxContainer.new()
+	row.size_flags_vertical = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
+	row.add_theme_constant_override("separation", 14)
+	root.add_child(row)
+	row.add_child(rail(current, go, keys))
+	var sep := VSeparator.new()
+	row.add_child(sep)
+	var col := VBoxContainer.new()
+	col.size_flags_horizontal = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
+	col.size_flags_vertical = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
+	col.add_theme_constant_override("separation", 10)
+	row.add_child(col)
+	return col
+
+
+## The Talos host (editor_screen.gd: every tool kept, switched by showing
+## one), or null when a tool runs as a scene of its own (tests).
+static func host(tree: SceneTree) -> Node:
+	var s := tree.current_scene
+	return s if s != null and s.has_method("show_tool") else null
+
+
+## The rail's click from a tool: in the host, straight there (the tool stays
+## as it is, so nothing to ask); on its own, `guard` first (it asks about
+## unsaved changes, then calls what it's given), then the tool's scene.
+static func go(tree: SceneTree, id: String, guard := Callable()) -> void:
+	var h := host(tree)
+	if h:
+		h.show_tool(id)
+	elif guard.is_valid():
+		guard.call(func(): open(tree, id))
+	else:
+		open(tree, id)
+
+
+## A tool's scene: the one loaded in the background (_warm) if it's there.
+static func scene(path: String) -> PackedScene:
+	if ResourceLoader.load_threaded_get_status(path) != ResourceLoader.THREAD_LOAD_INVALID_RESOURCE:
+		var r := ResourceLoader.load_threaded_get(path)
+		if r is PackedScene:
+			return r
+	return load(path)
+
+
+## Goes to tool `id` (a data-editor page, a tool, or "menu").
+static func open(tree: SceneTree, id: String) -> void:
+	var h := host(tree)
+	if h:
+		h.show_tool(id)
+		return
+	if id in PAGES:
+		page = PAGES.find(id)
+		tree.change_scene_to_file(EDITOR)
+	elif SCENES.has(id):
+		tree.change_scene_to_file(SCENES[id])
+
+
+## A screen's header: its name (and a line under it, `note`, for status
+## messages) on the left; the screen's own buttons go after the spacer.
+## Returns [header, note label].
+static func header(title: String, note: String, accent: Color) -> Array:
+	var h := HBoxContainer.new()
+	h.add_theme_constant_override("separation", 8)
+	var t := UI.label(title, 24, accent)
+	t.name = "TalosTitle"
+	h.add_child(t)
+	var n := UI.label(note, 14, UI.TEXT_DIM)
+	n.name = "TalosNote"
+	n.size_flags_horizontal = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
+	n.clip_text = true
+	n.text_overrun_behavior = TextServer.OVERRUN_TRIM_ELLIPSIS
+	n.vertical_alignment = VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT_CENTER
+	h.add_child(n)
+	return [h, n]
+
+
+## The tools' shortcuts, wherever you are in Talos (before the tool's own keys:
+## Ctrl+digit isn't a room or a zoom here).
+class Keys extends Node:
+	var go: Callable
+	var current := ""
+
+	func _input(event: InputEvent) -> void:
+		var k := event as InputEventKey
+		if k == null or not k.pressed or k.echo or not is_visible_in_tree_safe():
+			return
+		var id := ""
+		if k.ctrl_pressed and k.keycode >= KEY_1 and k.keycode < KEY_1 + PAGES.size():
+			id = PAGES[k.keycode - KEY_1]
+		elif not k.ctrl_pressed:
+			id = {KEY_F3: "library", KEY_F4: "scenarios", KEY_F6: "svg", KEY_F7: "patcher"}.get(k.keycode, "")
+		if id == "" or id == current:
+			return
+		get_viewport().set_input_as_handled()
+		go.call(id)
+
+	func is_visible_in_tree_safe() -> bool:
+		var p := get_parent() as Control
+		return p != null and p.is_visible_in_tree()

files.explanation: Wrecks: what a destroyed ship or station leaves - its own sprite greyed, scorched and torn - to salvage with a Salvage Rig.

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,149 @@ 
+class_name Wreck
+extends Node2D
+## What a destroyed ship or station leaves behind: its own sprite, greyed out,
+## scorched and torn open (shaders/wreck.gdshader), drifting and turning
+## slowly. With a Salvage Rig fitted (Items.EQUIPMENT "salvage_rig") you can
+## salvage it: click it - the ship flies up and cuts it apart (main.gd:
+## _update_salvage, SALVAGE_TIME) - for scrap and parts, now and then a piece
+## of gear, and the Electro emitter of a ship that had one (salvage()).
+## Wrecks aren't saved; they drift away after LIFE seconds (a station's
+## stays longer), MAX of them in a system at once.
+
+const MAX := 14
+const LIFE_SHIP := 300.0
+const LIFE_STATION := 900.0
+const FADE := 4.0
+## Close enough to cut it (from its edge).
+const SALVAGE_REACH := 320.0
+const SALVAGE_TIME_SHIP := 4.0
+const SALVAGE_TIME_STATION := 10.0
+## A ship with an Electro gives it up this often.
+const ELECTRO_SALVAGE := 0.6
+
+static var _shader: Shader
+
+var kind := "ship"            # "ship" / "station"
+var title := ""               # what it was ("Spartan Hoplite-class Gunship", "Kastor Phalanx")
+var empire := ""
+var toughness := 100.0        # its hull (and shields): the bigger, the more salvage
+var electro := false
+var radius := 60.0            # roughly (for clicking it, and the salvage reach)
+var progress := 0.0           # salvaging: seconds of cutting done
+var salvaged := false
+var _life := 0.0
+var _spin := 0.0
+var _drift := Vector2.ZERO
+var _sprite: Sprite2D
+var _mat: ShaderMaterial
+
+
+## Leaves a wreck at `at` (global) under `host` (the space scene): `tex` drawn
+## at `scl`, turned `rot`. `info`: kind, title, empire, toughness, electro.
+## Null without a texture.
+static func spawn(host: Node, at: Vector2, tex: Texture2D, scl: Vector2, rot: float, info: Dictionary) -> Wreck:
+	if tex == null or host == null or not host.is_inside_tree():
+		return null
+	var all := host.get_tree().get_nodes_in_group("wrecks")
+	if all.size() >= MAX:
+		all[0].queue_free()   # (the oldest drifts off)
+	var w := Wreck.new()
+	w.kind = str(info.get("kind", "ship"))
+	w.title = str(info.get("title", "ship"))
+	w.empire = str(info.get("empire", ""))
+	w.toughness = float(info.get("toughness", 100.0))
+	w.electro = bool(info.get("electro", false))
+	w.radius = maxf(tex.get_width() * absf(scl.x), tex.get_height() * absf(scl.y)) * 0.42
+	w._sprite = Sprite2D.new()
+	w._sprite.texture = tex
+	w._sprite.scale = scl
+	w.rotation = rot
+	host.add_child(w)
+	w.global_position = at
+	return w
+
+
+func _ready() -> void:
+	add_to_group("wrecks")
+	z_index = -2
+	if _shader == null:
+		_shader = load("res://shaders/wreck.gdshader")
+	_mat = ShaderMaterial.new()
+	_mat.shader = _shader
+	_mat.set_shader_parameter("seed", randf() * 100.0)
+	_mat.set_shader_parameter("burn", randf_range(0.35, 0.8) if kind == "ship" else randf_range(0.5, 0.9))
+	if _sprite:
+		_sprite.material = _mat
+		add_child(_sprite)
+	_spin = randf_range(-0.12, 0.12) if kind == "ship" else randf_range(-0.02, 0.02)
+	_drift = Vector2.from_angle(randf() * TAU) * (randf_range(6.0, 18.0) if kind == "ship" else 2.0)
+
+
+func life() -> float:
+	return LIFE_STATION if kind == "station" else LIFE_SHIP
+
+
+func salvage_time() -> float:
+	return SALVAGE_TIME_STATION if kind == "station" else SALVAGE_TIME_SHIP
+
+
+func _process(delta: float) -> void:
+	_life += delta
+	rotation += _spin * delta
+	position += _drift * delta
+	var left := life() - _life
+	if left < FADE:
+		_mat.set_shader_parameter("fade", clampf(left / FADE, 0.0, 1.0))
+		if left <= 0.0:
+			queue_free()
+
+
+## Cut apart: what it gives drifts out (Pickup - tractor it in); the wreck
+## falls to pieces. Returns what it was, for the log.
+func salvage(data: Node) -> String:
+	if salvaged:
+		return ""
+	salvaged = true
+	var rng := RandomNumberGenerator.new()
+	rng.randomize()
+	var level := clampf(toughness / 900.0, 0.0, 1.0)
+	var drops := []
+	var gear_rolls := 0
+	if kind == "station":
+		drops = [["scrap", rng.randi_range(14, 24)], ["machinery", rng.randi_range(2, 5)], ["electronics", rng.randi_range(1, 4)],
+			["alien_alloy", rng.randi_range(0, 2)], ["fuel", rng.randi_range(2, 6)]]
+		gear_rolls = 2
+		level = 0.7
+	else:
+		drops = [["scrap", 2 + int(level * 6.0) + rng.randi_range(0, 2)]]
+		if rng.randf() < 0.35:
+			drops.append(["electronics", rng.randi_range(1, 2)])
+		if rng.randf() < 0.25:

+## A Library rock, drawn into a small view of its own and shown from there:
+## the rock shader (ray-marched, lit, noise on noise) on 34 big rocks at once
+## took the room's GPU to 4.3 ms a frame. The rocks only turn slowly (a few
+## thousandths of a radian between redraws), so each is redrawn REFRESH times
+## a second, a few each frame in turn (~0.4 ms each): the same to the eye,
+## the room ~1.8 ms a frame. Live edits reach the rock's material as before.
+class RockView extends Node2D:
+	static var _all: Array = []
+	static var _next := 0
+	static var _frame := -1
+	static var _due := 0.0
+	const REFRESH := 20.0
+	var _vp: SubViewport
+
+	static func wrap(rock: Control) -> RockView:
+		var v := RockView.new()
+		var full := rock.size
+		var res := Vector2i((full * 0.6).clamp(Vector2(96, 96), Vector2(640, 640)))
+		v._vp = SubViewport.new()
+		v._vp.size = res
+		v._vp.transparent_bg = true
+		v._vp.render_target_update_mode = SubViewport.UPDATE_ONCE
+		rock.position = Vector2.ZERO
+		rock.size = Vector2(res)
+		v._vp.add_child(rock)
+		v.add_child(v._vp)
+		var spr := Sprite2D.new()
+		spr.texture = v._vp.get_texture()
+		spr.scale = full / Vector2(res)
+		v.add_child(spr)
+		return v
+
+	func _enter_tree() -> void:
+		_all.append(self)
+
+	func _exit_tree() -> void:
+		_all.erase(self)
+
+	func _process(d: float) -> void:
+		# (the first rock to run each frame asks the next few to redraw)
+		if _frame == Engine.get_process_frames():
+			return
+		_frame = Engine.get_process_frames()
+		var n := _all.size()
+		_due += n * REFRESH * minf(d, 0.1)
+		var count := int(_due)
+		_due -= count
+		for i in mini(count, n):
+			_next = (_next + 1) % maxi(1, n)
+			var r: RockView = _all[_next]
+			if is_instance_valid(r) and r._vp:
+				r._vp.render_target_update_mode = SubViewport.UPDATE_ONCE

+extends TestCase
+## Save slots (SaveGame: SLOTS of them, a summary each, the old single save
+## moved into slot 1) and saving on a planet (you load back down there, where
+## you stood).
+
+
+func setup() -> void:
+	for i in range(1, SaveGame.SLOTS + 1):
+		SaveGame.delete_slot(i)
+	Galaxy.new_game(false)
+
+
+func teardown() -> void:
+	for i in range(1, SaveGame.SLOTS + 1):
+		SaveGame.delete_slot(i)
+	SaveGame.pending = {}
+	SaveGame.resume = {}
+	SaveGame.landed_planet = ""
+	SaveGame.space_state = {}
+	SaveGame.travelling = false
+
+
+func test_slots() -> void:
+	check(not SaveGame.has_save(), "no saves")
+	check(SaveGame.save_game({"player": {"credits": 111}}, 2), "saved in slot 2")
+	await tree.create_timer(1.1).timeout   # (the newest by its time stamp)
+	check(SaveGame.save_game({"player": {"credits": 333}}, 5), "saved in slot 5")
+	check(SaveGame.has_save(2) and SaveGame.has_save(5) and not SaveGame.has_save(1), "two slots used")
+	check_eq(SaveGame.latest_slot(), 5, "the newest")
+	var info := SaveGame.slot_info(2)
+	check_eq(int(info["summary"]["credits"]), 111, "a slot's summary: credits")
+	check(str(info["summary"]["system"]) != "", "and where you were")
+	check(SaveGame.queue_load(2) and int(SaveGame.pending["player"]["credits"]) == 111, "load a chosen slot")
+	check(SaveGame.queue_load() and int(SaveGame.pending["player"]["credits"]) == 333, "load the newest")
+	SaveGame.delete_slot(5)
+	check(not SaveGame.has_save(5), "deleted")
+	check(SaveGame.slot_info(4).is_empty(), "an empty slot")
+
+
+func test_old_save_becomes_slot_1() -> void:
+	var f := FileAccess.open(SaveGame.LEGACY, FileAccess.WRITE)
+	f.store_string(JSON.stringify({"version": 1, "saved_at": "2026-01-01T10:00:00", "state": {"player": {"credits": 77}}}))
+	f.close()
+	SaveGame._migrate()
+	check(not FileAccess.file_exists(SaveGame.LEGACY), "the old file moved")
+	check(SaveGame.has_save(1) and int(SaveGame.read_save(1)["state"]["player"]["credits"]) == 77, "into slot 1")

+func test_save_on_a_planet() -> void:
+	SaveGame.space_state = {}

+	var s: Node = load("res://scenes/planet_surface.tscn").instantiate()
+	tree.root.add_child(s)
+	while not s.is_built:

+	var where: Vector2 = s.pilot.position
+	var d: Dictionary = s.get_save_data()
+	check(d.has("landed") and d["landed"]["planet"] == "thalassa", "a save on a planet says which")
+	check(Vector2(d["landed"]["pos"][0], d["landed"]["pos"][1]).is_equal_approx(where), "and where you stood")
+	check(SaveGame.save_game(d, 3), "saved")
+	check(str(SaveGame.slot_info(3)["summary"]["planet"]) != "", "the slot list shows the planet")
+	s.queue_free()
+	await tree.process_frame
+	# Loading it: the space scene sets up the landing ...
+	SaveGame.landed_planet = ""
+	SaveGame.queue_load(3)
+	var main: Node = load("res://main.tscn").instantiate()
+	tree.root.add_child(main)

+	check(SaveGame.QUICK in SaveGame.all_slots() and SaveGame.AUTO in SaveGame.all_slots(), "both in the load list")
+	check(SaveGame.latest_slot() in [SaveGame.QUICK, SaveGame.AUTO], "the newest of them")
+	check(SaveGame.queue_load(SaveGame.QUICK) and not SaveGame.pending.is_empty(), "the quicksave loads")
+	SaveGame.pending = {}
+	# Under attack: no autosave.

+	main.queue_free()

+func test_autosave_settings() -> void:
+	var old_m: int = Settings.autosave_minutes
+	var old_e: bool = Settings.autosave_events

+	check(not SaveGame.has_save(SaveGame.AUTO), "periodic autosaves off: none")
+	check(SaveGame._auto_t <= 0.0, "(the timer doesn't run)")

+	menu._autosave_option.item_selected.emit(Settings.AUTOSAVE_CHOICES.find(15))
+	check_eq(Settings.autosave_minutes, 15, "chosen there")
